description:
pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs ParseError has two variants that wrap foreign error types:

* `ParseError::AddFailed { index: usize, source: DeviationAddError }` (line 154)
* `ParseError::InvalidParameterOverride { param_id: String, source: ParameterError }` (referenced in lib.rs:1444)

Neither has a `From<DeviationAddError>` or `From<ParameterError>` impl. Result: every call site that wants to propagate has to spell out the wrap by hand:

```rust
store.add(dev).map_err(|source| ParseError::AddFailed { index: idx, source })?;
clone.set_parameter(...).map_err(|source| ParseError::InvalidParameterOverride { param_id: ..., source })?;
```

The wrapping is mechanical and adds boilerplate. For `AddFailed` specifically the additional context (`index`) is what blocks a naïve `From` impl — without the index, the variant cannot be reconstructed. That is a real reason; not every error wrap is From-able.

But at minimum:

* The author could ship a constructor: `impl ParseError { fn from_add_failed(index: usize, source: DeviationAddError) -> Self }` so call sites read `store.add(dev).map_err(|e| ParseError::from_add_failed(idx, e))?` — same boilerplate but at least the variant construction is centralised.
* Or restructure so the index lives in the call-site context (e.g., a fresh `ParseError::AddFailed` that doesn't carry index, with the index recorded separately).

The canonical anti-pattern from the error-handling section: 'Error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields' — this isn't that exactly, but it's the cousin: 'Error variants that wrap structured errors without providing the ergonomic `?`-friendly conversion.' Pre-1.0 there is room to redesign; post-1.0 the boilerplate gets locked in.

File is P2: not a correctness issue, real ergonomic tax on every internal call site, fix is a redesign that wants thinking-time rather than mechanical fixing.
title: oscal::parse::ParseError wraps DeviationAddError and ParameterError but ships no From impls — forces .map_err() at every call site
